title: Ontology-Agent Tool Schemas
description: JSON Schema mirrors for common IDE / agent tools. Extend per project. Used by Layer 1 (type check) before Layer 2 (shape check) in scripts/validate_tool_call.py. Copy this file to <project-root>/.ontology-agent/schema/tools.json and adjust per project (bootstrap.py, owned by the ontology-core sibling piece, does this automatically). The x-shape-target and x-property-map keys are optional data hooks read by the generic shape evaluator: x-shape-target names which shape (by targetClass, from schema/shapes.json) the tool's arguments should be validated against; x-property-map renames a JSON argument key to the ontology property path it represents when the names differ. Neither key changes Layer 1 semantics — plain JSON Schema validators can ignore them. Default-deny: any tool_name NOT listed under 'properties' below is rejected by validate_tool_call.py's Layer 1 (code 'unregistered_tool'), never silently allowed through. The only sanctioned opt-out is marking a tool's entry 'x-unvalidated: true' with a required, non-empty 'x-unvalidated-reason' string -- see 'x-unvalidated-escape-hatch-example' below for the exact shape (documentation only; not itself a live tool entry, since type_check only reads 'properties'). Every example tool actually registered below is fully schema'd; none opts out by default.

path.description: Relative or absolute path inside the workspace

query_graph.description: Mirrors scripts/query_graph.py's actual CLI: fixed subcommands over an entity_id/task_id and --depth, not SPARQL -- there is no SPARQL engine anywhere in this skill.

entity_id.description: The entity_id (contains/depends-on/subgraph) or task_id (blocked-by/blocking) to query.

depth.description: Hop limit. depends-on: unbounded if omitted. subgraph: defaults to 2. Ignored by contains/blocked-by/blocking.

json.description: Print raw JSON instead of a formatted summary (matches the --json flag).

graph_path.description: Optional override path to graph.jsonl (matches --graph). Default: search upward from cwd for .ontology-agent/graph.jsonl.

x-unvalidated-escape-hatch-example.$comment: Documentation only -- not a live tool entry (validate_tool_call.py's type_check only reads the 'properties' object above). Copy a shape like this INTO 'properties' if you have a genuinely pure read-only/exploratory tool that a project owner has consciously decided doesn't need type/shape gating. Both keys are required for the escape hatch to take effect: x-unvalidated must be exactly `true`, and x-unvalidated-reason must be a non-empty string -- a missing or empty x-unvalidated-reason fails closed (the tool is rejected, same as an unregistered one), it does not silently grant the opt-out.

grep_search.x-unvalidated-reason: Pure read-only text search across the workspace; no state mutation for the gate to check.
